answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and stands that color's Player ID card visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set with that color on its backs; remove cards targeting colors not in play and keep the player's own Ambush card. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center with their values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: “stands its Player ID card visibly in front of them”; “Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing. Keep your own Ambush card”; “Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center; keep their values hidden.”

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player turn order. A player may change their face-down choice until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and “reveal all choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is necessary. Red is the sole Target because Red received the most votes (three); the rule is a plurality threshold, with every player tied for the most votes also becoming a Target.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.”

answers.answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes, and without successful Ambush protection both are eliminated. A player may satisfy the voting requirement by voting for either tied Target.
answers.evidence: Vote: tied players “are Targets”; “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.” Targets are eliminated unless protected by their own successful Ambush.

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the Target (Blue), and receiving no votes does not protect Green. Green's vote for Red does not satisfy the requirement to vote for a Target.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated,” subject to the successful Ambush exception.

answers.answer: Ambush does not count as a vote. Yellow's vote gives Red one vote, and Pink's vote gives Yellow one vote, so Red and Yellow tie for most votes and both are Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds because Red is a Target; Red survives and may eliminate one player who voted for Red, which is Yellow. Pink survives because Pink voted for a Target (Yellow). Among the named players, Red and Pink survive; Yellow is eliminated.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Ambush cards do not count as votes”; tied leaders “are Targets.” Ambush: a Target's successful Ambush lets them “choose one of the players who voted for them to eliminate.” With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.

answers.answer: No. They eliminate exactly one of the players who voted for them, even if four did so. They cannot choose a player who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: the ambusher chooses “one of the players who voted for them”; “They cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.”

answers.answer: The player eliminates themselves. An Ambush by someone who is not a Target fails.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, continue with another Conspire → Vote → Resolve cycle, and only the surviving players participate in the next vote.
answers.evidence: Survivors table: “Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.”

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points; each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: Survivors table: “One | That survivor collects all four central Gold Bars.” Components: “receiving one bar means receiving one card whose value is 3, 4, or 5 points.”

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go; they may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card and places it face down. When both are ready, they reveal simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: each takes “a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go”; each chooses one face down, and “reveal both choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. The players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome. Leave the four central bars in place for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Survivors table: “Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.” Special Rules clarifies final voters “receive no consolation bar for that outcome.”

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The Share player gets zero central bars and the Steal player gets all four.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Steal: “You get 0; opponent gets 4.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar, and the Steal player receives three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Steal: “You get 1; opponent gets 3.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar, and the Share player receives three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Grab One & Go: “You get 3; opponent gets 1.”

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one bar; two bars remain in the center. If play continues, deal just two new bars, bringing the central pool to four.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: if both choose Grab One & Go, “each finalist receives one central bar. Leave the remaining two in the center and add just two new bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: if both choose Steal, “neither finalist receives gold”; “give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck”; “Leave all four central bars for the next round, and give no new gold.”

answers.answer: Check for victory at the end of each round, after Gold Bars are awarded. With 6–9 players the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring: “Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; “If more than one player has reached the threshold, the highest point total wins.”

answers.answer: For exactly two qualifying players tied for the highest Gold point total, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown. Repeat Showdowns as necessary until one player has the highest total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated during that round; stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
answers.evidence: Scoring: “If the highest qualifying totals are tied, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown” and “Repeat these Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total.” Turn Structure: “everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.”
